title: How to use dictation in Pages on Mac: step by step for Pages 15.4
metaTitle: How to use dictation in Pages on Mac: steps for 2026
description: Learn how to use dictation in Pages on Mac: choose Edit > Start Dictation, speak your text, then click Done. Includes fixes for common problems.
targetKeyword: how to use dictation in pages on mac
intro: To use dictation in Pages on Mac, open your document, place the insertion point where the text should go, and choose Edit > Start Dictation. Speak when the microphone appears, say punctuation names such as comma, and click Done below the microphone when you finish.
tldr: Click where the text should go, or select the words you want to replace, before you start.
Choose Edit > Start Dictation, or press the Microphone key, then speak when the microphone appears.
Say punctuation by name, such as comma or apostrophe.
Click Done below the microphone, or press Escape, to stop.
If nothing happens, check Dictation in System Settings > Keyboard and your input volume.

blocks.text: Before you start: check which Pages you have

Apple's Pages user guide for Mac says it covers Pages 15.4, and the steps in this guide follow that version. Pages has two editions on the Mac, so the version number on your machine matters. Open Pages, choose Pages > About Pages, and read the version number before you follow any steps.

In late January 2026, Apple updated the old Mac app to version 14.5 and said it would no longer get new features. New features now arrive in the Apple Creator Studio edition of Pages, which started at version 15.1. If you still run 14.5, check the Edit menu for Start Dictation before you go further. This guide cannot promise that every menu matches in older builds.
Wikipedia lists 15.4 as the latest release, but its version history table skips that number. Treat any version number as a moving target, and trust what your own About window shows.
Turn on Dictation and choose your language

Dictation has its own settings, separate from Pages. Open the Apple menu, choose System Settings, click Keyboard in the sidebar, then open Dictation. You will see an on or off switch, a Shortcut menu with a Customize option, a Languages button, a Microphone source menu, and an Auto-punctuation option.
Set the language before you start. If your document is in one language, pick that language in the Languages list. Changing it later works, but it is one more step you can skip if you set it now.

items: Dictation: switched on, so the feature is available in Pages.
Shortcut: note the key you press, so you know how to start and stop it.
Languages: the language your document is written in.
Microphone source: Automatic is the default. Change it only if you use an external microphone.
Auto-punctuation: test one sentence with it on and one with it off, then keep the setting you prefer.

blocks.text: Start dictation from the Edit menu, the Microphone key or a shortcut

Pages gives you three ways to start dictation. The Edit menu route is the one Apple documents for Pages. The Microphone key on your keyboard starts dictation too, and so does the Dictation shortcut you set in Keyboard settings. A quick press and release of the Microphone key starts dictation. Press and hold it, and you get Siri instead.

rows: The route in Apple's Pages guide
Press the key you set in Keyboard settings
Change it under System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation

blocks.text: Speak punctuation and choose where the text goes

Speak at a normal pace. For punctuation, say the name of the mark. Apple's Pages guide uses comma and apostrophe as examples, so say the word comma when you want a comma in the text. Keep sentences short when you start, so you can see how the app handles your voice before you draft a long section.

Placement matters more than most people expect. Dictation writes at the insertion point. If you select words before you start, the new speech replaces the selection. Click once where the new text belongs, then start dictation. Select text only when you want the new speech to overwrite it.
Stop dictation and check what you wrote

Click Done below the microphone when you finish. Escape, the Microphone key, or your Dictation shortcut also stops it. Read the paragraph back before you move on. Check names, numbers, and words that sound alike, because speech input can mishear them, and those mistakes are easy to miss at speaking speed.
How long dictation runs before it stops

Dictation has no fixed limit on the length of your text. It does stop by itself after 30 seconds with no detected speech. If you pause to think, the microphone may close before you are ready. Start it again from Edit > Start Dictation, and the next words land at the insertion point.
Typing while dictation is on

On Macs with Apple silicon, you can keep typing while dictation is active. The cursor pauses its pulsing while you type, then resumes when you stop. This helps when you want to fix one word in the middle of a sentence. The Apple text I checked does not cover Intel Macs for this, so test it before you rely on it.
Apple Intelligence on macOS 27

Apple says macOS 27 adds an on-device model to Dictation. The model improves spelling, punctuation and capitalization. Apple lists English as the supported language and Mac models with M3 or later, with at least 12GB of unified memory. If your Mac does not meet those limits, check Apple's help page before you expect the upgrade.
Dictation not working in Pages? Start with the checklist

Apple's troubleshooting page for Dictation is short. Work through it in order, because the first items are the quickest to check. Each item below comes from that checklist, so a failure in one area usually shows up in one place.

items: Dictation is switched on in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation.
The language matches the text you want to write.
The shortcut you press is the one you set.
The input volume under Sound > Input is high enough for your microphone.
Background noise is low enough for the microphone to hear your voice.

blocks.text: Apple's checklist does not include a restart step. Some third-party guides suggest restarting, or switching Dictation off and on again. That can help, but it is not Apple's advice. If Voice Control is on, standard Dictation is not available, so turn Voice Control off first.
Which Pages edition gets new features

The Pages app you open decides which features you see. Apple's newsroom says Keynote, Pages, Numbers and Freeform will remain free for all users to create, edit and collaborate. The paid part is Apple Creator Studio, at $12.99 per month or $129 per year. New subscribers get a one-month free trial.

MacRumors reports that the Creator Studio edition of Pages adds premium templates, a Content Hub, AI-based image tools and larger iCloud collaboration files. Those extras are separate from dictation. The sources I checked do not list dictation as a Creator Studio feature.
Is dictation faster than typing?

A 2016 arXiv preprint by Ruan and colleagues found that English speech input was 3.0x faster than keyboard input on a smartphone. The same study reported a 20.4% lower English error rate. That study tested phones, not Pages on a Mac, so treat it as a rough signal. It still helps when you decide whether dictation is worth the setup time for a long draft.
Mistakes people make with dictation in Pages

items: Starting in the wrong place. Click where the text belongs before you press Start Dictation.
Selecting a word by accident, then watching the speech replace it.
Expecting the next sentence to appear after you click Done. Start dictation again to continue.
Speaking to the wrong input. Check the Microphone source setting if your voice is quiet or missing.
Dictating a long draft without reading it back, then finding the errors days later.

blocks.text: What to do after you dictate a draft

Once the draft is down, switch from speaking to editing. If an editor needs to see your changes, [turn on Track Changes in Pages on Mac](/how-to/turn-on-track-changes-in-pages) first. For notes to yourself, [add a comment in Pages on Mac](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-pages) keeps them attached to the text they describe.

If you send the file to someone who uses Word, [save as a Word file in Pages on Mac](/how-to/save-as-a-word-file-in-pages) before you share it. If you write for a living, the usual pattern is draft by voice, read the text aloud, then correct it by hand. The [dictation tips for writers](/for/writers) cover that workflow in more detail.

faq.question: Do I need to be online to use dictation in Pages?
faq.answer: Apple's troubleshooting checklist includes your network connection, so a weak connection is one thing to rule out. The Apple pages I checked do not say whether dictation works offline in every language, so test it before a long session.

faq.question: Why does dictation stop on its own in Pages?
faq.answer: Dictation stops automatically after 30 seconds with no detected speech. Start it again from Edit > Start Dictation or with the Microphone key, then keep writing from the same insertion point.

faq.question: How do I stop dictation in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: Click Done below the microphone, or press Escape, the Microphone key, or your Dictation shortcut. Any of these ends the session.

faq.question: Can I dictate over text I already wrote?
faq.answer: Yes, but select the text first. Apple's Pages guide says new speech replaces the selected text, so a stray selection will be overwritten without warning.

faq.question: Does dictation work in Pages for iCloud in a browser?
faq.answer: I could not confirm this from the sources I checked. Apple's Pages guide covers the Mac app, and the iCloud version had no dictation steps in the pages I opened. Use the Mac app for the steps in this guide.

faq.question: Which languages does dictation support in Pages?
faq.answer: Apple's Pages guide does not list supported languages. Open System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation and check the Languages list on your Mac, since that list controls what your Mac uses.

faq.question: Do I need Apple Creator Studio to use dictation in Pages?
faq.answer: Apple's newsroom says Pages remains free for all users to create, edit and collaborate. Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year and adds premium templates. The sources I checked do not list dictation as a Creator Studio feature.

task: Dictate text into a Pages document on Mac
appliesTo: Pages for Mac 15.4 on macOS with Dictation turned on
requirements: Pages open with a document you can edit
Dictation turned on in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation
A working microphone, such as the built-in one
A network connection, as Apple's troubleshooting checklist suggests

steps.name: Open your document and place the cursor
steps.text: Open the Pages document. Click once where the new text should go. If you want to replace words, select them first, because the dictated text replaces the selection.
steps.tip: Click on an empty line before a new paragraph. It is easier than fixing spacing later.

steps.name: Choose Edit > Start Dictation
steps.text: Open the Edit menu in the menu bar at the top of the screen, then choose Start Dictation. The microphone appears when dictation is ready to take your speech.
steps.tip: The Microphone key on your keyboard starts dictation too. Press and release it.

steps.name: Finish the guided setup if it appears
steps.text: If you have not used dictation before, Pages walks you through a guided setup. Follow the prompts until the setup ends, then start dictation again from the Edit menu.

steps.name: Speak when the microphone appears
steps.text: Speak at a normal pace in the language you set. Your words appear at the insertion point as you talk, one sentence at a time.

steps.name: Say punctuation by name
steps.text: Say the name of a mark when you want it in the text. Apple's Pages guide uses comma and apostrophe as examples, so say the word comma for a comma.

steps.name: Stop with Done or Escape
steps.text: Click Done below the microphone when you finish. You can also press Escape, the Microphone key, or your Dictation shortcut to stop dictation.

steps.name: Check the text and correct it
steps.text: Read the dictated text back, or scroll through it. Fix names, numbers, and words that sound alike. Then keep editing with the keyboard and trackpad.
steps.tip: Turn on Track Changes first if someone else will review the draft.

steps.name: Change the shortcut or language if needed
steps.text: Open the Apple menu, choose System Settings, click Keyboard in the sidebar, then open Dictation. Use the Shortcut menu to set a key, or use the Languages button to change the language.

shortcuts.action: Start or stop dictation with your shortcut
Start dictation with the Microphone key

troubleshooting.problem: Dictation stops before I finish speaking
troubleshooting.fix: Dictation stops after 30 seconds with no detected speech. Start it again from Edit > Start Dictation and continue at the same insertion point. The text you already dictated stays in the document.

troubleshooting.problem: The microphone never appears in Pages
troubleshooting.fix: Check that Dictation is on in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation, then confirm the language and shortcut. Apple's checklist also covers the external microphone input volume under Sound > Input.

troubleshooting.problem: Dictation is missing from the Edit menu
troubleshooting.fix: Check your version in Pages > About Pages, since Apple's guide covers 15.4. Also turn off Voice Control, because standard Dictation is not available while it is on.
Speak more slowly, check the language setting, and reduce background noise. On macOS 27 with an M3 or later Mac and at least 12GB of memory, the on-device model improves spelling and punctuation.
